description: Narrative of adoptee's search for birth family or birth family's search for placed child. Specific identity-and-origin search register.
exemplars: Jeanette Winterson's Why Be Happy When You Could Be Normal?; Dani Shapiro's Inheritance; A.M. Homes's The Mistress's Daughter; modern DNA-discovery memoirs.

name: Family Estrangement Narrative
description: Narrative of cutting off a family member or being cut off — typically with detailed reasoning and emotional cost. Specific family-rupture register.
exemplars: Jeanette Winterson; Justine Bateman's writings; modern essays on parental estrangement; many trauma memoirs.

name: Parenting Memoir
description: First-person narrative of becoming and being a parent. Specific parental-experience register.
exemplars: Anne Lamott's Operating Instructions; Andrew Solomon's Far from the Tree; Rivka Galchen's Little Labors; many modern parenting memoirs.

name: Friendship Memoir / Eulogy
description: First-person account of a particular friendship and what it meant. Friendship as central frame.
exemplars: Michelle Tea's writings; Roxane Gay on Roxana; many essay collections featuring friendship memoir; Tuesdays with Morrie (variant).

name: Patient Story (medical communication)
beats: What patients want healthcare to know
description: First-person account of a patient's medical experience, often used in medical education or advocacy. Specific medical-system perspective.
exemplars: Patient stories in NEJM's "Perspective"; Health Affairs narratives; advocacy organization patient stories.

name: Doctor-Writer Narrative
description: Physician's first-person account of clinical practice — patients, system, ethical dilemmas. Distinct from patient story by physician's perspective and authority.
exemplars: Atul Gawande's essays; Oliver Sacks's case studies; Abraham Verghese; Lisa Sanders's Diagnosis column; Siddhartha Mukherjee.

name: Therapy Session Reconstruction
description: Narrative reconstruction of psychotherapy sessions — specific therapeutic-encounter register. Common in popular psychology writing.
exemplars: Irvin Yalom's Love's Executioner; Stephen Grosz's The Examined Life; Lori Gottlieb's Maybe You Should Talk to Someone.

name: War Memoir (combat)
description: First-person account of combat experience by a veteran. Specific combatant-perspective register.
exemplars: Tim O'Brien's The Things They Carried (in part); Karl Marlantes's What It Is Like to Go to War; Phil Klay's Redeployment; Erich Maria Remarque's All Quiet on the Western Front.

name: War Correspondence / Front-Line Reportage
description: Journalistic reporting from active war zones. Specific reportorial-from-combat register.
exemplars: Ernie Pyle's WWII columns; Michael Herr's Dispatches (Vietnam); Anna Politkovskaya's Chechnya reporting; Marie Colvin's reports; Sebastian Junger's War.

name: Battle Narrative (historical)
description: Detailed reconstruction of a historical battle — strategy, tactics, individual stories. Specific military-historical scope.
exemplars: Stephen Ambrose's Citizen Soldiers; Cornelius Ryan's The Longest Day; James M. McPherson's Civil War battle narratives; Antony Beevor's WWII books.

name: Resistance Narrative
description: Narrative of resistance against occupation, oppression, or tyranny. Specific underground-defiance register.
exemplars: Anne Frank's Diary; Hans Fallada's Every Man Dies Alone; Schindler's List (Keneally); WWII French Resistance narratives; Inglourious Basterds (fictional variant).

name: POW Narrative
description: Account of imprisonment as prisoner of war. Specific captivity-and-survival register.
exemplars: Louis Zamperini's story (Unbroken, Hillenbrand); Eugene Sledge's With the Old Breed; Stephen Ambrose; Boris Pasternak prisoner-themes.

name: Military Strategic Analysis
description: Analytical writing on military strategy, doctrine, or campaign. Prescriptive-analytical register distinct from history.
exemplars: Carl von Clausewitz's On War; modern RAND reports; war college analyses; Foreign Affairs strategy pieces.

name: Veteran Reintegration Narrative
beats: Sustained civilian life or continued struggle
description: Account of veteran's return to civilian life — psychological, social, professional reintegration. Specific post-deployment register.
exemplars: Brian Turner's My Life as a Foreign Country; American Sniper (post-war material); Kevin Powers's The Yellow Birds; Karl Marlantes.

name: Unit History / Military Group Narrative
description: Narrative tracing a specific military unit through its formation, deployments, and dissolution. Specifically collective-unit register.
exemplars: Stephen Ambrose's Band of Brothers (Easy Company); James McPherson's regimental histories; modern military unit chronicles.

name: Counterinsurgency / Asymmetric Warfare Narrative
description: Narrative of unconventional warfare — guerilla fighters, occupation, counterinsurgency. Specific asymmetric register.
exemplars: Sebastian Junger's War; Restrepo (documentary); Generation Kill (Wright); The Outpost (Tapper); Vietnam-era counterinsurgency literature.

name: Atrocity / War Crime Narrative
beats: The atrocity itself (often by careful telling)
description: Narrative documenting wartime atrocities — by witness, survivor, investigator, or perpetrator. Specific moral-witness register.
exemplars: Philip Gourevitch's We Wish to Inform You That Tomorrow We Will Be Killed With Our Families (Rwanda); Hiroshima (Hersey); My Lai accounts; The Things They Carried episodes.

name: Adventure Travel Narrative
description: Travel narrative emphasizing physical adventure — climbing, sailing, jungle expedition. Distinguished from generic travel by danger-stakes register.
exemplars: Jon Krakauer's Into the Wild and Into Thin Air; Sebastian Junger's The Perfect Storm; Tim Cahill's adventure travel.

name: Cultural Travel Essay
description: Travel writing focused on encountering specific culture, language, or place. Anthropological-essayistic register distinct from adventure.
exemplars: Pico Iyer's travel writing; Bruce Chatwin; Paul Theroux; Sara Wheeler; Granta travel issues.

name: Volunteer / Service Travel Narrative
description: Travel narrative of volunteer or service work in another place — Peace Corps, NGO, missionary. Service-engagement register; often interrogating motives.
exemplars: Sarah Erdman's Nine Hills to Nambonkaha; Shantaram (variant); modern Peace Corps memoirs; critical NGO-experience writings.

name: Place-Based Memoir
description: Memoir centered on the author's relationship to a specific place over time — neighborhood, region, landscape. Place as primary frame.
exemplars: Annie Dillard's An American Childhood; Eudora Welty's One Writer's Beginnings; Robert Macfarlane; Helen Macdonald's Vesper Flights.

name: Restaurant Review
beats: Final recommendation with stars or rating
description: Critical review of a restaurant — atmosphere, service, food, value. Specific dining-evaluation register.
exemplars: NYT restaurant reviews (Pete Wells); Michelin Guide; Eater; classical restaurant criticism.

name: Recipe Narrative
description: Recipe presented within a personal/cultural narrative frame — origin story, family memory, cultural context — followed by the actual recipe instructions.
exemplars: Modern food blogs (Smitten Kitchen); Samin Nosrat's Salt Fat Acid Heat; Food52; NYT Cooking; many ethnic-food cookbooks.

name: Cookbook Narrative
description: Long-form cookbook with sustained narrative, philosophy, or biographical thread alongside recipes. Narrative ambition distinct from recipe-collection cookbook.
exemplars: Julia Child's Mastering the Art of French Cooking; Marcella Hazan; Edna Lewis's The Taste of Country Cooking; Yotam Ottolenghi's books; Madhur Jaffrey.

name: Hunger / Body Memoir
beats: Early relationship with food and body
description: Memoir centered on the author's complicated relationship with food, body, hunger. Specifically embodied-disordered register.
exemplars: Roxane Gay's Hunger; Caroline Knapp's Appetites; Marya Hornbacher's Wasted; An Apple a Day (Emma Woolf).

name: Popular Science Book
beats: Scientific question or field framed accessibly
description: Long-form book translating scientific findings or fields for general audiences. Bridging-academic-and-popular register.
exemplars: Stephen Hawking's A Brief History of Time; Richard Dawkins's The Selfish Gene; Mary Roach's books; Bill Bryson's A Short History of Nearly Everything; Carl Sagan.

name: Science Magazine Feature
beats: Hook (often human story or vivid scene)
description: Long-form magazine article on scientific topic. Length and journalistic-magazine register distinct from popular-science book.
exemplars: Wired features; Atlantic science features; Quanta Magazine; New Yorker science pieces.

name: Citizen Science Narrative
description: Narrative of non-scientist volunteers contributing to scientific research — biodiversity counts, astronomical observation, archaeological discovery.
exemplars: eBird-related narratives; iNaturalist project stories; SETI@home accounts; Galaxy Zoo discoveries.

name: Climate Narrative / Eco-Reportage
description: Long-form narrative reporting on climate change — its causes, effects, responses. Non-fiction commitment distinct from cli-fi.
exemplars: Elizabeth Kolbert's The Sixth Extinction; David Wallace-Wells's The Uninhabitable Earth; Naomi Klein's This Changes Everything; Bill McKibben's writings.

name: Environmental Writing
beats: History of human relationship with it
description: Long-form writing on environmental themes — wilderness, conservation, ecological loss. Specifically political-environmental register.
exemplars: Aldo Leopold's A Sand County Almanac; Edward Abbey's Desert Solitaire; Wendell Berry's essays; Robin Wall Kimmerer's Braiding Sweetgrass.

name: Conservation Narrative
description: Narrative of conservation effort — saving species, protecting land, restoring ecosystem. Conservation-success-or-struggle register.
exemplars: American Buffalo (Burns documentary); Jane Goodall's chimp work; The Whale and the Reactor (Winner); California condor recovery narratives.

name: Deep-Time / Geological Narrative
description: Writing exploring deep geological or cosmic time — how landscapes formed, how species evolved, how the universe will end. Time-scale-shifting register.
exemplars: John McPhee's Annals of the Former World; Robert Macfarlane's Underland; Annie Dillard's deep-time passages.

name: The Quiet Pivot
description: A protagonist undergoes a small but irreversible internal change without external announcement. The change is real but unaccompanied by ceremony or public statement. Use when the meaningful turn happens privately.
exemplars: Many literary-fiction interior turns; quiet-resignation arcs; mid-life recalibration essays.

name: Recognition Without Words
beats: Tension or distance held between two
Meeting of eyes or shared moment
description: Two characters arrive at understanding without speaking. The change is mutual and silent — the recognition itself is the structural payoff.
exemplars: Many film moments (the long look); literary-fiction reconciliation scenes; certain estrangement-end moments.

name: Inheritance Refused
beats: Recognition of what taking it would cost
description: Receiving a legacy — money, authority, family role, ideological mantle — and choosing not to take it. Distinct from rejection (hot) by being quiet and respectful.
exemplars: Family-business successor narratives; ideological-second-generation refusals; literary "leaving the firm" arcs.

name: The Return-to-Origin
beats: Return seeing what once was, differently
description: A protagonist comes back to where they began — physically, relationally, vocationally — and sees it transformed by their own change. Use when the genre's content is the gap between memory and present perception.
exemplars: Hometown-return memoirs; reunion scenes in literary fiction; Annie Dillard's An American Childhood register.

name: Found Through Loss
beats: Recognition that the loss made the finding possible
description: What was sought is gained only through losing something else. The structural insight is the inversion: the gain was hidden inside the loss.
exemplars: Recovery memoirs where bottom enables sobriety; vocational-reinvention essays; certain grief-memoir resolutions.

name: Permission Granted
description: Receiving — from elder, mentor, partner, or self — the right to do what one already wanted. The genre's payoff is the *release* the permission unlocks.
exemplars: Coming-of-age threshold scenes; retirement-permission narratives; mid-life "you can stop now" arcs.

name: The Naming
beats: Name uttered for the first time
description: Calling something by its true name for the first time. The act of naming is the structural pivot — what was diffuse becomes addressable.
exemplars: Diagnosis moments; "I'm queer" / "I'm an alcoholic" / "this is abuse" identification arcs; many therapeutic breakthroughs.

name: Companion-in-the-Dark
description: Sustained presence through another's worst time without trying to fix. The genre's content is loyalty-as-witness rather than loyalty-as-action.
exemplars: Many caregiver-narrative quiet sequences; deep-friendship grief arcs; therapeutic-presence narratives.

name: Unannounced Mastery
beats: Quiet doing of the difficult thing
description: Quiet competence revealed without performance. The protagonist does the hard thing without announcement; recognition (if it comes) is incidental.
exemplars: Workplace quiet-excellence narratives; behind-the-scenes hero stories; many older-craftsman profiles.

name: The Belated Apology
description: Apology delivered years after the wound. The genre's content is what late accountability is and isn't — and the recipient's right to whatever response.
exemplars: Reconciliation memoirs; long-deferred-letter narratives; modern accountability essays.

name: Tender Surrender
description: Letting something go without struggle, with affection. Distinct from defeat (hot) and from refusal (firm) — the release is *kind*.
exemplars: End-of-relationship scenes that are not breakups; closing-of-a-business arcs; child-leaves-home narratives in their soft form.

name: Borrowed Light
beats: Need for strength one does not yet have
Borrowed strength from another's wisdom or example
description: Living temporarily inside another's wisdom or grace until one's own arrives. The structural insight is that borrowed strength can become real.
exemplars: Mentorship-period memoirs; therapy-narrative sequences; "she believed in me until I could" arcs.

name: The Hand Held Out
description: Offering help that may or may not be accepted. The genre's payoff is the *offer itself* — the value is in extending the hand, not in the result.
exemplars: Outreach-to-estranged-family essays; reaching-back-to-former-self narratives; many small kindness anecdotes.

name: Unfinished Business
description: Acknowledging that some things will never close. Distinct from closure (resolution) and from denial (avoidance) — the protagonist learns to *live alongside* the unfinished.
exemplars: Late-grief memoirs; certain estrangement narratives; long-illness reflective essays.

name: The Witnessing Circle
beats: Crisis or wound brought to community
Group bears witness without trying to fix
Something restored by the act of witnessing
description: Communal acknowledgment that creates change without action. The collective presence is itself the intervention. Distinct from group therapy (which intervenes) by emphasizing pure witness.
exemplars: Truth and Reconciliation Commission narratives; Quaker meeting moments; some recovery-meeting structures; certain grief-circle traditions.

name: Kathāsaritsāgara frame-tale (कथासरित्सागर)
beats: Outer frame story established (often a king, sage, or supernatural figure)
Tales nest inside tales (often three or four deep)
Each tale illustrates a moral or wisdom
Resolution returns through nested layers to the frame
description: 11th-century Sanskrit "Ocean of Stories" frame-tale collection by Somadeva. Foundational to Indian frame-narrative tradition; influenced Pañchatantra and Arabian Nights.
exemplars: Somadeva's Kathāsaritsāgara; Bṛhatkathā tradition; Vetāla Pañcaviṃśati (25 tales of the vampire).

name: Sufi Qissa narrative (قصة)
description: Sufi spiritual tale of seeker-and-master, paradox-and-insight. Distinct from generic Sufi parable by longer, more elaborated narrative arc.
exemplars: Tales in Attar's Conference of the Birds; Rumi's narrative passages in Masnavi; classical qissa collections.

name: Hikaya (Arabic short tale, حكاية)
description: Short Arabic tale form — typically a single anecdote with a moral or surprising turn. Distinct from longer dastan or maqama by compression.
exemplars: Tales within Thousand and One Nights (the shorter ones); al-Tanukhi's Nishwar al-Muhadara anecdotes; Ibn al-Jawzi's collections.

name: Aboriginal Dreamtime narrative
beats: Land features formed by the action
Ongoing relationship between living people and the Dreaming
description: Australian Aboriginal narrative of the Dreaming (Tjukurrpa, Alcheringa, etc.) — ancestral beings shape Country through their journeys; living people continue these stories. Sacred and place-specific.
exemplars: Yolngu Songlines; Pitjantjatjara Tjukurrpa narratives; Bruce Chatwin's Songlines (external account); modern Indigenous-authored versions.
notes: Sacred to specific peoples; this entry documents the structural form, not protected ritual content.

name: Maori whakapapa narrative
beats: Origin (Te Kore, Te Pō, Te Ao Mārama)
Ancestral lineage traced from primordial parents
Connection to land (whenua), tribe (iwi), and present speaker
description: Maori (New Zealand) genealogical narrative form — recitation of descent from primordial origins through ancestors to the speaker, establishing identity and standing.
exemplars: Maori whakapapa recitations; oral tradition documented in Buck's The Coming of the Maori; modern Maori-authored sources.

name: Polynesian moʻolelo (voyage narrative)
beats: Reading of stars, currents, and birds
Genealogical connection from voyager to present
description: Polynesian wayfinding-and-settlement narrative — voyaging across vast Pacific distances, claiming and naming islands, establishing lineages.
exemplars: Hawaiian moʻolelo of Hawaiʻi-loa; Cook Islands voyage narratives; Marquesan and Tahitian wayfinding traditions; modern Hokuleʻa documentation.

name: Kebra Nagast narrative (Ethiopian)
beats: Encounter between Solomon and Queen of Sheba
Return with the Ark of the Covenant
Founding of the Solomonic dynasty in Ethiopia
description: Ethiopian "Glory of the Kings" — foundational narrative of the Solomonic dynasty, integrating biblical origin with Ethiopian sovereignty and the Ark.
exemplars: Kebra Nagast text (14th-c. compilation, older traditions); modern Ethiopian Orthodox liturgical recitations.

name: Swahili utenzi epic
description: Swahili long narrative poem, typically Islamic-heroic in subject. Composed in quatrains; often celebrating prophetic figures, battles, or moral heroes.
exemplars: Utenzi wa Tambuka (Epic of Heraclius); Utenzi wa Liyongo; Islamic Swahili poetic tradition (East African coast, 17th c. onward).

name: Akan Anansesem (formal Anansi tales)
beats: Opening formula ("My story which I am about to tell, let it come, let it go")
Action against larger figure (sky-god, lion, elephant)
description: Formal Akan storytelling tradition with stock opening and closing formulae. Distinct from generic Anansi cycle by its specific performative-frame conventions.
exemplars: Akan oral storytelling tradition (Ghana, Ivory Coast); R.S. Rattray's Akan-Ashanti Folk-Tales (1930); modern Asante storytelling.

name: Igbo Ifo folk narrative
beats: Opening call-and-response between teller and audience
Animal or human character with desire or transgression
description: Igbo (Nigeria) folk narrative form, typically performed orally with audience participation. Often features tortoise (Mbe) as trickster; etiological or moral.
exemplars: Tortoise stories collected in Achebe's Things Fall Apart and No Longer at Ease; modern Igbo folkloric collections; Nwapa's Idu and Efuru.

name: Quechua / Andean origin narrative
beats: Manco Cápac and Mama Ocllo emerge from Lake Titicaca
Connection to present land and people
description: Andean origin narrative — Inca founding myth and broader Quechua cosmology. Specific connection to landscape (apus, huacas) and sacred geography.
exemplars: Inca Garcilaso de la Vega's Royal Commentaries; Felipe Guamán Poma de Ayala's Nueva crónica; modern Quechua oral tradition.

name: Mapuche oral narrative (Epeu)
description: Mapuche (Chile/Argentina) oral narrative form. Epeu (story) and ngütram (historical narrative) are distinct sub-forms.
exemplars: Mapuche oral tradition documented by Manuel Mansilla and others; modern Mapudungun-language collections.

name: Aztec codex narrative
description: Aztec/Mexica historical-mythological narrative form, originally pictorial-textual codices. Records origin, migration, dynastic succession, and prophecy.
exemplars: Codex Boturini (Tira de la Peregrinación); Florentine Codex (Sahagún); Codex Mendoza; modern Mexica-authored reconstructions.

name: Russian skazka (folk tale)
beats: Opening "In a certain kingdom, in a certain land..."
Encounter with magical helper (Baba Yaga, firebird)
"And I was there, and drank mead and wine..." closing
description: Russian folk-tale tradition — distinct from broader European folk-tale by specific stock figures (Baba Yaga, Koshchei the Deathless, Ivan-Tsarevich) and characteristic openings/closings.
exemplars: Afanasyev's Russian Folk-Tales; Pushkin's verse adaptations; Bilibin illustrations; modern Russian-language collections.
notes: Categorized as Celtic-Norse for European-Slavic placement; could be its own tradition in future expansion.

name: Persian Shāhnāmeh / Book of Kings
description: Ferdowsi's 10th-c. Persian national epic — 50,000 couplets covering kings and heroes from creation to Sasanian fall. Foundation of Persian literary identity.
exemplars: Ferdowsi's Shāhnāmeh; Dick Davis's English translation; modern Persian editions and recitations.

name: Tibetan Gesar epic
beats: Series of campaigns against demonic forces
description: Central Asian / Tibetan / Mongolian oral epic — longest in the world, with millions of lines across versions. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
exemplars: Tibetan Gesar tradition; Mongolian Geser; Buryat versions; living oral epic with master-singers (drungba).
notes: Categorized as Indigenous-Americas placeholder for Inner Asian tradition; could be its own category in future.

name: Mongolian heroic epic (tuuli)
beats: Battles with monsters or rival khans
description: Mongolian long narrative poem (tuuli, ülger) performed by epic-singers (tuulchin) with khoomei (throat-singing) and morin khuur (horse-head fiddle).
exemplars: Jangar epic; Geser cycle (Mongolian variant); Khalkha and Oirat oral traditions; modern UNESCO documentation.

name: Filipino Hudhud / Ifugao epic
description: Ifugao (Philippines) chanted oral epic, performed during rice-harvest and ritual occasions. UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage.
exemplars: Hudhud chants of the Ifugao (Cordillera); Manuel Dulawan's collections; modern Ifugao cultural preservation.

name: Yiddish folk narrative
beats: Ordinary Jewish protagonist (often a fool, scholar, or wise woman)
Lesson rooted in Jewish ethical-religious tradition
description: Yiddish folk-tale tradition (Eastern European Jewish) — shtetl life, golems, dybbuks, Hasidic tales, Chelm fool stories. Specific cultural-religious context.
exemplars: I.B. Singer's stories; tales of Chelm; Chassidic rabbinic narratives; Hershele Ostropoler; The Dybbuk (S. An-sky).
notes: Categorized under Celtic-Norse for European placement; deserves own tradition in future expansion.

name: Romani oral narrative
beats: Outcome that affirms Romani identity or wisdom
description: Romani folk-narrative tradition — wandering, outsider-perspective, often featuring trickster motifs and Romani moral framing distinct from settled European traditions.
exemplars: Romani oral collections by Ian Hancock and others; modern Romani-authored literature; tales documented across European Romani communities.

name: Apology (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat compressed apology — for short conversational, social-media, or direct-message contexts. Distinct from formal apology letter (612) by compression.
exemplars: Effective public apology tweets; brief in-conversation apologies; therapeutic accountability sentences.

name: Brag (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Frame that lets the recipient celebrate without awkwardness
description: 3-beat self-celebration shape — sharing accomplishment in a way that invites others in rather than alienates. Distinct from boast by tonal awareness.
exemplars: Effective LinkedIn announcement posts; casual-text celebrations; "humble brag" done well.

name: Reveal (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Crack — first sign of something underneath
description: 3-beat shape for disclosing a hidden truth — about a person, situation, or product. Universal communicative arc for unmasking.
exemplars: Investigative-tweet threads; product-flaw disclosures; personal-disclosure micro-essays.

name: Lesson Learned (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for the most basic teaching narrative — what I used to think, what happened, what I think now. Common in advice content, personal essays, professional reflections.
exemplars: "What I learned from..." posts; advice-column structure; mentoring micro-stories.

name: Recommendation (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Resolve — why it solves the problem
description: 3-beat shape for recommending a product, book, person, place. Most basic structure for word-of-mouth.
exemplars: Product reviews; book recommendations; "you should try..." messages.

name: Complaint (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for grievance — to a company, institution, or person. Specifies what was promised, what happened, what's owed.
exemplars: Customer complaints; HR grievances; political letters of complaint; angry tweets that work.

name: Gratitude (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Recognition of what it cost the giver or what it meant
description: 3-beat shape for thanks — distinct from formal thank-you by being conversational and immediate. The structural payoff is the relationship the gratitude creates.
exemplars: Effective thank-you texts; team appreciation messages; intimate gratitude expressions.

name: Confession (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for telling someone something hidden — affair, lie, mistake, identity. Distinct from formal confession by conversational immediacy.
exemplars: Coming-out conversations; "I have to tell you something..." disclosures; therapeutic confessions.

name: Hot Take (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Why it matters or what changes
description: 3-beat shape for the contrarian opinion — most common rhetorical move on social media, in op-eds, in conversations. Provocation done well.
exemplars: Effective Twitter hot-take threads; opinion-essay leads; "actually..." conversations done thoughtfully.

name: Pivot (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Was — old direction, identity, or commitment
description: 3-beat shape for announcing a change — career, project, position, identity. Distinct from career pivot narrative by extreme compression.
exemplars: "I'm leaving X to do Y" announcements; brand pivot communications; personal transition posts.

name: Realization (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for the small epiphany — the conversational "I just realized..." moment. Most basic structure for sharing personal revelation.
exemplars: Casual "I just realized..." texts; therapy-breakthrough recountings; reflective journal entries.

name: Goodbye (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for parting — leaving a job, ending a friendship, closing a chapter. Brief, dignified, and forward-tilted.
exemplars: Farewell emails; closing speeches; intimate goodbyes; retirement announcements.

name: Greeting (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for opening conversation, message, or relationship. Most common structure for first-contact communications.
exemplars: Effective cold introductions; networking openers; rekindling-old-contact messages.

name: Sales Pitch (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for selling — product, service, idea. Most basic conversion structure.
exemplars: Effective ad copy; landing-page hero sections; brief sales emails; elevator pitches.

name: Origin Story (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for short-form origin — brand, project, person, decision. Distinct from full Brand Origin Story by compression.
exemplars: About-page bios; LinkedIn summaries; brand intro videos; founder Twitter threads.

name: Win (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for celebrating an achievement — sporting, professional, personal. Most basic triumph structure.
exemplars: "We did it!" announcements; sports recaps; project-win communications.

name: Loss (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for facing an unwanted outcome — election loss, project failure, sporting defeat. Dignified acknowledgment.
exemplars: Concession statements; project-failure debriefs; public-loss acknowledgments.

name: Comeback (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Fall — what was lost or wrong
description: 3-beat shape for short-form comeback narrative. Distinct from full comeback narrative by compression.
exemplars: "I'm back" posts; recovery-from-injury announcements; relaunch-after-failure communications.

name: Explainer (3-beat)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Why — why it matters or exists
How — how it works or what to do
description: 3-beat shape for short explanation — concept, product, process. Most basic explainer structure.
exemplars: Quick-explainer tweets; product-feature one-liners; concept introductions.

name: Resignation (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for the most compressed resignation — distinct from formal resignation letter (615) by extreme brevity. Useful for verbal or text resignations.
exemplars: Brief resignation statements; verbal notice patterns; text-message resignations (controversial but common).

name: Welcome (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for welcoming — new hire, new resident, new member. Distinct from greeting by being directional (toward community).
exemplars: New-hire welcome messages; subscriber welcome emails; community-onboarding announcements.

name: Refusal (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for saying no — preserving relationship while declining. Most basic boundary-without-rupture structure.
exemplars: "Thanks but no" messages; polite project declines; saying-no-to-meetings emails.

name: Promise (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for making a promise — distinct from generic statement of intent by including the accountability frame.
exemplars: Manager commitments to direct reports; brand promises; relationship promises.

name: Warning (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for warning someone — about a person, situation, or risk. Distinguished from cautionary tale by compression and direct-recipient orientation.
exemplars: Warning messages between friends; institutional safety alerts; product-recall communications.

name: Endorsement (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for short-form endorsement. Distinct from testimonial appeal (200) by being conversational rather than advertising.
exemplars: Personal recommendations; political endorsements (compressed); social-media praise posts.

name: Excuse (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Implied or stated request for understanding
description: 3-beat shape for the explanation-of-failure that isn't quite an apology. Distinct from apology by externalizing cause; common but ethically loaded.
exemplars: Late-to-meeting explanations; missed-deadline messages; everyday social explanations.
notes: Useful as a recognized shape; ethical use depends on whether the external cause is genuine.

name: Confidence-Building (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for building someone's confidence — colleague before a presentation, child before an exam. Distinct from generic encouragement by specific-evidence beat.
exemplars: Pre-game coach talks; mentor-to-mentee texts; manager-to-direct-report messages before stretch assignments.

name: Boundary-Setting (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Affirmation of continuing connection within new limit
description: 3-beat shape for setting a boundary — with family, partner, colleague. Distinct from refusal by being relational/ongoing rather than transactional.
exemplars: Therapeutic-conversation boundary statements; modern relational-health communications; workplace boundary messages.

name: Question Held (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat compressed version of "The Held Question" (306) — for short-form contexts. Conversational shape for declining to resolve while staying engaged.
exemplars: Skilled therapist responses; Socratic conversation moves; thoughtful not-yet-answer statements.

name: Quiet Defiance (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for refusing to comply without making it a fight. Distinct from confrontation; the resistance is in the *continuation*.
exemplars: Civil-disobedience statements; quiet-refusal-of-authority messages; "I respectfully disagree and will continue..." communications.

name: Claim-and-Evidence (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for short argumentative content — distinct from full Toulmin model (130) by compression. Most basic persuasive structure.
exemplars: Effective short opinion pieces; brief persuasive emails; one-sentence-thesis arguments.

name: Reframe (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for changing how something is being thought about — distinct from hot take by being constructive rather than provocative.
exemplars: Coaching reframes; therapeutic reframes; brand-positioning shifts; political-message reframes.

name: Public Stance (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
description: 3-beat shape for taking a public stand — on a political issue, social moment, or institutional question. Most basic structure for going on the record.
exemplars: CEO statements on social issues; celebrity stance-taking; institutional-position communications.

name: Witness Statement (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: What it means for the record
description: 3-beat shape for testimony or eyewitness account — distinct from formal testimony by compression. Useful for journalism, social movements, accountability.
exemplars: Effective eyewitness tweets; brief court-testimony summaries; activist witness statements.

name: Plea (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINAL GENRES — Communicative 3-Beat Shapes (Phase 7 seeds)
beats: Recognition of the audience's power to decide
description: 3-beat shape for asking someone to do something they could refuse — reduce a sentence, donate, vote, forgive. Distinct from sales pitch by emphasis on the asker's vulnerability.
exemplars: Sentencing-statement pleas; fundraising messages; victim-impact statements; reconciliation requests.

name: Pep Talk
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Affirmation of capability and prior wins
description: Compressed motivational shape for pre-game, pre-presentation, pre-launch moments. Distinct from generic encouragement by its action-orienting close.
exemplars: Coach pep talks; manager rallies; pre-meeting team huddles; speech before the speech.

name: Setting Expectations
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for clarifying what the recipient should anticipate. Distinct from promise by being mutual rather than one-directional.
exemplars: Manager-direct-report opening conversations; therapist-client first session; vendor-client kickoff messages.

name: Calling Out
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: Public criticism shape — direct, on-the-record, intended to create pressure for change. Distinct from quiet conversation by public posture.
exemplars: Twitter callouts; institutional-accountability statements; political confrontations.

name: Calling In
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of the relationship and shared values
Invitation to reflect and do better
description: Private criticism shape — distinct from calling out by being relational rather than public. Aims at growth rather than pressure.
exemplars: Loretta Ross's calling-in framework; close-friendship corrections; mentor private feedback.

name: Defending Someone
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that the person has been attacked or misrepresented
description: 3-beat shape for stepping in for someone — colleague being misrepresented, friend in conflict, someone falsely accused.
exemplars: Workplace defense moments; friend-defending-friend interventions; public statements of solidarity.

name: Asking for Help
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for requesting assistance — distinct from generic request by including the why-you specifically beat.
exemplars: Help requests in professional contexts; vulnerable asks; community-support solicitations.

name: Asking for Advice
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What would be most useful from the advisor
description: 3-beat shape for soliciting advice — distinct from asking for help by being decision-oriented rather than action-oriented.
exemplars: Mentor consultations; "what would you do?" conversations; structured advice asks.

name: Negotiation Opening
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Acknowledgment of mutual interest in agreement
description: 3-beat shape for opening a negotiation. Frames the conversation as collaborative-problem-solving rather than zero-sum.
exemplars: Salary negotiation openings; vendor contract discussions; policy negotiations.

name: Negotiation Close
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Summary of where both sides have moved
description: 3-beat shape for closing a deal. Locks in agreement clearly and orients toward implementation.
exemplars: Deal-closing messages; HR final-offer communications; sales-close conversations.

name: Counter-Offer
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Why the revision serves both parties
description: 3-beat shape for proposing alternative terms. Preserves relationship while renegotiating.
exemplars: Salary counter-offers; vendor counter-proposals; real-estate counter-offers.

name: Walk-Back / Retraction
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Reference to prior statement or position
Acknowledgment that it was wrong or premature
description: 3-beat shape for correcting a public statement. Distinct from apology by focusing on the position rather than the harm.
exemplars: Corporate clarifications; public-figure walk-backs; corrections to prior reporting.

name: Denial (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of the accusation or claim
description: 3-beat shape for denying an accusation. Most basic structure for refuting publicly.
exemplars: Public-figure denials of wrongdoing; corporate denials of accusations; personal disputes.

name: Doubling Down
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for refusing to back down under pressure. Ethically loaded — useful when the original position deserves defense.
exemplars: Political statements after pushback; brand re-commitments; principled stands under criticism.

name: Curiosity Expression
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of something unfamiliar or surprising
description: 3-beat shape for genuine inquiry. Distinct from question-as-rhetorical-move by signaling actual receptivity.
exemplars: Genuine curiosity in conversation; ethnographic-mode questions; child-like inquiry as adult communication.

name: Status Update
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What has been done since last update
What is blocked or coming next
description: 3-beat shape for project status — distinct from progress report by being conversational and current. Standard agile/operating cadence.
exemplars: Standup meeting updates; project-status emails; progress messages to stakeholders.

name: Reminder
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Reference to prior commitment or context
description: 3-beat shape for nudging without nagging. Most basic structure for productive follow-up.
exemplars: Calendar reminders; gentle follow-up emails; deadline nudges.

name: Heads-Up
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What recipient might want to do
description: 3-beat shape for proactive information-sharing. Distinct from generic FYI by including recipient-action beat.
exemplars: "FYI before this hits your inbox..." messages; insider warning communications; courtesy-update conversations.

name: Synthesis
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of multiple positions or inputs
description: 3-beat shape for pulling together a discussion's threads. The structural payoff is the integration, not new content.
exemplars: Meeting-closing summaries; thought-leadership integrations; mediator interventions.

name: Compliment (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What it conveys about the person
description: 3-beat shape for genuine praise — distinct from generic compliment by being specific and inferential.
exemplars: Effective performance-feedback praise; relational compliments; mentor-affirmation messages.

name: Constructive Criticism
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for feedback that grows rather than diminishes. Distinct from calling out by being private and developmental.
exemplars: Manager feedback to direct reports; teacher feedback on student work; peer-review comments.

name: Validation (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Acknowledgment of what the other is feeling or experiencing
Affirmation that the response makes sense
description: 3-beat shape for emotional validation — distinct from advice by deliberately not fixing. Therapeutic and relational core skill.
exemplars: Therapist responses; effective parental validation; close-friendship support messages.

name: Empathic Reflection
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Listen to what the other has said
Open question or invitation to continue
description: 3-beat shape for active listening. Distinct from validation by reflecting content as well as feeling.
exemplars: Coaching conversation moves; therapeutic listening; effective conflict-mediation patterns.

name: Setting Context
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that the recipient may not know the background
description: 3-beat shape for orienting someone before a request, decision, or conversation. Most basic structure for "let me bring you up to speed."
exemplars: Pre-meeting briefings; "before we get into this..." conversations; new-to-the-team onboarding moments.

name: Diffusing Tension
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for stepping into and reducing conflict. Distinct from validation by being situational rather than sustained.
exemplars: Mediator interventions; effective de-escalation in arguments; conflict-resolution moves.

name: Acknowledging Someone's Win
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What it took to get there
description: 3-beat shape for honoring someone else's success — distinct from generic congratulations by recognizing the work.
exemplars: Promotion congratulations; project-completion celebrations; relationship-milestone acknowledgments.

name: Sharing Good News
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: What it means or what's next
description: 3-beat shape for sharing a positive development. Distinct from win by being broader (life events, not just achievements).
exemplars: Engagement announcements; promotion shares; pregnancy reveals; project-launch posts.

name: Sharing Difficult News
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Acknowledgment that this is hard to share
What support or response is needed
description: 3-beat shape for delivering bad or hard news — distinct from confession by being external (not self-disclosure) rather than internal.
exemplars: Layoff notifications; medical-news shares with family; loss-of-loved-one announcements.

name: Inviting to Event
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for inviting — distinct from announcement by being recipient-specific.
exemplars: Wedding invitations; conference invitations; personal-event invitations.

name: Declining an Invitation
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for declining gracefully. Distinct from refusal by being relational and warm.
exemplars: Polite RSVP-no messages; declining work-event invitations while preserving relationships.

name: Confirming Attendance
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Anticipation or specific question about logistics
description: 3-beat shape for accepting and engaging with an invitation. Specific and warm rather than generic.
exemplars: RSVP-yes messages; meeting confirmations; event acknowledgments.

name: Re-engagement After Silence
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of the time that has passed
Specific reason for reaching out now
description: 3-beat shape for restarting a dormant relationship — friendship, professional connection, family contact. Acknowledges the gap honestly.
exemplars: "It's been a while..." messages; LinkedIn reconnection notes; family-reach-out communications.

name: Disagreement With Respect
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for disagreeing without rupture. Distinct from refutation by emphasizing relational continuity.
exemplars: Mature professional disagreements; family political conversations; principled-but-civil debates.

name: Self-Deprecation Done Well
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for owning a flaw with humor — without self-flagellation. Builds connection through honesty.
exemplars: Effective comedic memoir; conversational charm; brand "we screwed up" honesty.

name: Vulnerability Share
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that this is hard to share
What is being asked of the listener (often: just to receive)
description: 3-beat shape for sharing emotional truth. Distinct from confession by being current and continuing rather than retrospective.
exemplars: Therapeutic disclosures; intimate-relationship vulnerability; brave-public-statement vulnerabilities.

name: Curiosity-Invitation
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that the other might be interested
description: 3-beat shape for inviting someone into a conversation, project, or experience without forcing. Low-pressure outreach.
exemplars: Casual connection invitations; "would you ever want to..." messages; soft-pitch communications.

name: Wisdom-Passing
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition of the recipient's question or situation
description: 3-beat shape for offering hard-won insight — distinct from advice by being more about disclosure than prescription.
exemplars: Elder-to-younger-generation conversations; mentor disclosure of past mistakes; veteran professionals' counsel to newcomers.

name: Memory-Sharing
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Connection to present moment or recipient
description: 3-beat shape for sharing a memory — at a funeral, anniversary, or quiet moment. Distinct from storytelling by intimacy and present-tense relevance.
exemplars: Eulogy memory-passages; anniversary reflections; intimate memory-shares between long-known people.

name: Acknowledging the Elephant in the Room
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that something unspoken is in the room
description: 3-beat shape for breaking conversational avoidance. The structural payoff is the relief of the named.
exemplars: Therapy-breakthrough moments; team-meeting honesty; family-gathering courage.

name: "How Can I Help"
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Specific frame — what kinds of help are available
description: 3-beat shape for offering support without overstepping. Distinct from generic offer by being concrete about what's on offer.
exemplars: Effective grief-support messages; team-support offers; community mutual-aid communications.

name: Inquiry into Wellbeing
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that something has happened or might be happening
Acknowledgment that no answer is required
description: 3-beat shape for the genuine "are you okay?" message. Distinct from generic check-in by specificity and pressure-release.
exemplars: Friend check-ins after difficulty; manager wellness inquiries; thoughtful "thinking of you" messages.

name: Forgiveness-Asked
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Recognition that the answer is not owed
description: 3-beat shape for asking forgiveness. Distinct from apology by explicitly seeking absolution while acknowledging it's not earned.
exemplars: Reconciliation-conversation requests; restorative-justice statements; intimate-relationship repair attempts.

name: Forgiveness-Granted
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for granting forgiveness — distinct from generic acceptance by including the forward frame.
exemplars: Truth-and-Reconciliation testimony responses; intimate-relationship forgiveness moments; therapeutic-letter exercises.

name: Distance / Space-Asked
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Specific need for distance or break
Frame for what continues or how to reconnect
description: 3-beat shape for asking for space without rupture. Distinct from boundary-setting by being temporary.
exemplars: Relationship pause communications; family-space requests; therapeutic-break discussions.

name: Coming Closer
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
description: 3-beat shape for moving toward someone after distance. Distinct from re-engagement by being more intimate.
exemplars: "I miss you" messages done well; reconciliation-initiation communications; tender bid-for-closeness.

name: Patience-Asked
section: NGC ORIGINALS — More 3-Beat Communicative Shapes (Phase 7 continued)
beats: Acknowledgment that the other is waiting
Realistic frame for when resolution is coming
description: 3-beat shape for asking for time. Distinct from generic update by being explicit about the request.
exemplars: Project-delay communications; "I'm working on it" messages with specifics; relationship "I need time" conversations.

name: Bengali Mangal-Kāvya
description: Bengali narrative-poem genre (15th-18th c.) celebrating Hindu deities — Manasa (snake goddess), Chandi, Dharmaraj. Established devotional cults through narrative.
exemplars: Manasa-mangal; Chandi-mangal; Dharma-mangal; Mukundaram's Chandi-mangal.

name: Vedic Hymn-Narrative
beats: Invocation of deity or cosmic principle
description: Sanskrit Vedic hymn form — narrative content embedded in invocational poetry. Foundational South Asian sacred-narrative form.
exemplars: Rigveda hymns (especially to Indra, Agni, Soma); Atharvaveda; later Upanishadic narrative passages.

name: Tamil Bhakti narrative (Tevaram, Tiruvaymoli)
beats: Visit to specific shrine or sacred place
Encounter with the deity (Shiva or Vishnu)
description: Tamil devotional narrative tradition (7th-10th c. Nayanmars and Alvars) — pilgrimage-to-shrine narratives establishing major Shaiva and Vaishnava devotional traditions.
exemplars: Nayanmar Shaiva poetry (Tevaram); Alvar Vaishnava poetry (Divya Prabandham); Andal's Tiruppavai.

name: Hawaiian Mele (chant-narrative)
description: Hawaiian chanted narrative form — mele oli (chant) and mele hula (chant-with-dance). Carries genealogy, history, sacred knowledge.
exemplars: Kumulipo (Hawaiian creation chant); chants of specific places and rulers; modern Hawaiian language renaissance recitations.

name: Korean Sasol Sijo (long-form sijo)
description: Long-form variant of standard sijo (Genre 14), with extended middle section. Used for narrative poetry and ironic-comic content rather than meditation.
exemplars: Folk sasol sijo of the late Joseon period; modern Korean experimental sijo.

name: Mexican Corrido
description: Mexican narrative ballad form (19th-c. onward) — telling of revolutionary heroes, outlaws, border events. Specific six-section conventional structure.
exemplars: Corridos of the Mexican Revolution; Pancho Villa and Zapata corridos; modern narcocorridos (descended form).

name: Brazilian Cordel
description: Brazilian rhymed-verse pamphlet narrative tradition (Northeast, Sertão region). Sold at markets and fairs; printed on inexpensive paper. Folk literary form.
exemplars: Cordéis de cangaço (about banditry); Patativa do Assaré's writings; modern Brazilian cordel revival.

name: Andean Huayno Narrative-Song
beats: Personal address to beloved or community
description: Andean folk-musical narrative form (Quechua, Aymara). Combining song, dance, and personal-communal narrative. Foundational to Andean cultural identity.
exemplars: Traditional huayno across Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador; modern recordings (Pastorita Huaracina, Picaflor de los Andes).

name: Argentine Tango Narrative-Song
beats: Lover, mother, or city character introduced
description: Argentine tango lyrical-narrative form (early 20th c.). Specific Buenos Aires-rooted melancholy register; codified themes of loss, lust, exile.
exemplars: Carlos Gardel's tangos; "Mi Buenos Aires querido"; "Volver"; modern tango composers.

name: Cuban Son Narrative-Song
description: Cuban son musical-narrative form — fusion of African and Spanish elements. Foundational to Latin American popular music.
exemplars: Buena Vista Social Club; Trio Matamoros; Compay Segundo; Septeto Habanero.

name: Korean Sageuk variant — Pre-modern Romance
beats: Lovers across class or political lines
Tragic or triumphant resolution within Joseon constraints
description: Sub-form of Sageuk specifically focused on cross-class or politically-fraught romance. Distinct from broader court intrigue by foregrounding love story.
exemplars: Chunhyang-jeon (foundational Joseon-era pansori-novel); Sukhyangjeon; modern K-drama adaptations.

name: Vietnamese Truyện Kiều form
description: Vietnamese narrative-poetic form modeled on Nguyễn Du's Truyện Kiều (Tale of Kiều, early 19th c.) — foundational national epic, tragic heroine, Confucian-Buddhist moral framework.
exemplars: Nguyễn Du's Truyện Kiều; later Vietnamese narrative poetry in this lineage.
notes: Categorized as Indigenous-Americas placeholder for Vietnamese tradition; deserves its own East Asian-Southeast Asian category in future.

name: Burmese Yazawin Chronicle
description: Burmese royal-chronicle tradition — narrative history of kings within Buddhist cosmological framework. Combines mythic origin with historical succession.
exemplars: Glass Palace Chronicle (Hmannan Yazawin, 1832); earlier Mahayazawin; modern Burmese historical writing.

name: Thai Khmer Royal Epic (Ramakien)
description: Thai version of the Ramayana epic, adapted with local features. Foundational Thai narrative and dramatic tradition.
exemplars: Thai Ramakien; Cambodian Reamker; performed in khon dance-drama; widespread across Southeast Asia.

name: Yoruba Ifa Verse (Odu Ifa)
description: Specific elaborated form of Ifá divination narrative (related to Genre 53), recited verbatim by babalawo. Each of 256 odu has hundreds of memorized verses.
exemplars: Wande Abimbola's Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; living Yoruba Ifá practice; Cuban Lucumí variants.

name: Pivot-of-Direction
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of where we were headed
description: 3-beat shape for changing direction mid-conversation, mid-project, or mid-strategy. Distinct from pivot (745) by being situational rather than identity-based.
exemplars: Strategic redirect communications; mid-meeting course-correction moments; "actually, let's..." conversational turns.

name: Yes-And
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat improv-rooted communicative shape — distinct from generic agreement by explicit additive structure.
exemplars: Improv comedy moves; brainstorming sessions; collaborative-design conversations.

name: Holding-Two-Things
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for acknowledging contradiction without false resolution. Distinct from synthesis by explicitly refusing to integrate.
exemplars: Mature emotional conversations; therapeutic both-and statements; dialectical thinking moves.

name: Public Mourning (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for public mourning statement — distinct from eulogy by being short and platform-appropriate. Modern grief communication.
exemplars: Public mourning posts; collective-grief messages after disasters; community-loss acknowledgments.

name: Solidarity Statement (compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: What we will do (not just say)
description: 3-beat shape for solidarity that goes beyond posturing. Distinct from public stance by emphasis on action.
exemplars: Effective movement-solidarity statements; workplace allyship messages; community-support communications.

name: Ethical Reckoning
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for public ethical reckoning — distinct from apology by being ongoing, not just one-time. Common in modern accountability culture.
exemplars: Institutional reckoning statements; founder accountability posts; movement-leader course corrections.

name: Witness-from-Outside
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that the speaker is outside the affected group
Reframe in support of those affected
description: 3-beat shape for ally communication — when someone outside an experience speaks supportively about it. Specific about the speaker's positionality.
exemplars: Effective ally writing; ethnographic engagement; reportorial witness for marginalized communities.

name: Refusing-the-Frame
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the question or framing offered
Refusal to accept it as posed
description: 3-beat shape for declining a problematic question or framing — distinct from refusal (757) by intellectually re-framing rather than just saying no.
exemplars: Skilled interview moves; political deflection done well; therapeutic reframes refusing the patient's frame.

name: Moment-of-Acknowledgment
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what has just happened
description: 3-beat shape for stopping mid-conversation to acknowledge something important — distinct from synthesis by being interruptive rather than concluding.
exemplars: Therapeutic-conversation moves; "wait, can we just... " moments; presence-in-the-room communications.

name: Long-View Statement
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of immediate concern or pressure
Re-grounding in long-term values or vision
description: 3-beat shape for invoking the long view in short-term turbulence. Common in leadership communication during crisis.
exemplars: CEO crisis communications; coach pre-game centering; therapeutic perspective-shifting moves.

name: Cliffhanger (3-beat compressed)
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for serial-content cliffhanger — TV-episode close, podcast-episode end, social-media thread cliffhanger.
exemplars: Episode-end TV moments; "..." trailing in conversations; serial-story chapter ends.

name: Reveal-of-Self
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for self-disclosure that recontextualizes prior interactions. Distinct from confession by being relational pivot.
exemplars: Coming-out conversations; identity-disclosure moments; "I should tell you who I really am" arcs.

name: Naming-the-Pattern
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Implication of what to do about it
description: 3-beat shape for diagnostic recognition — workplace dynamic, relationship pattern, cultural trend. Naming creates leverage.
exemplars: Skilled coaching observations; cultural-criticism pieces; therapeutic insight moments.

name: Permission-to-Stop
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of how hard the recipient has tried
Specific permission to stop, rest, or let go
description: 3-beat shape for releasing someone from striving — distinct from generic comfort by giving specific permission. Therapeutic and pastoral core move.
exemplars: Caregiver-relief communications; therapeutic permission moments; pastoral-care statements.

name: Naming-What-Worked
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the achievement or moment
Specific element that made it work
description: 3-beat shape for identifying success factors — distinct from compliment by being analytical rather than affirmational.
exemplars: Effective retrospectives; coaching debriefs; product-launch post-mortems.

name: Choosing-What-to-Carry
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what could be carried forward
Conscious choice of what to keep
Release of what won't be carried
description: 3-beat shape for transitions — leaving a job, ending a relationship, finishing a project. Active choosing rather than passive losing.
exemplars: Year-end reflection content; transition-coaching moves; therapeutic letting-go conversations.

name: Quiet-Refusal-of-Pressure
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the pressure being applied
description: 3-beat shape for refusing manipulation, pressure, or coercion without escalation. Distinct from confrontation by gentleness.
exemplars: Skilled negotiation refusals; emotional-pressure deflections; political-pressure declines done with grace.

name: Acknowledgment-of-Complexity
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that this is more complex than usually presented
description: 3-beat shape for refusing simple framings without abandoning the issue. Common in thoughtful public discourse.
exemplars: Nuanced opinion pieces; mature-conversation moves; "it's complicated, AND..." statements.

name: Vow-Renewed
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Acknowledgment of how far we've come
description: 3-beat shape for re-committing to a long-term promise — wedding-anniversary, organizational mission renewal, personal-vow reaffirmation.
exemplars: Anniversary toasts; institutional-renewal speeches; year-end self-recommitment posts.

name: Witnessing-Beauty
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Sustained attention to a beautiful thing
description: 3-beat shape for noticing beauty — sunset, moment, person — without trying to capture or claim. Aesthetic-spiritual register.
exemplars: Nature-writing micro-passages; gratitude-journal entries; mindfulness-attention micro-essays.

name: Moment-of-Connection
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what is happening between two people
description: 3-beat shape for marking a moment of true connection — distinct from declaration of love by being more transient and recognized rather than promised.
exemplars: Quiet acknowledgments between friends; therapeutic alliance moments; intimate-relationship recognition.

name: Endurance-Acknowledged
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Acknowledgment of what it has taken
description: 3-beat shape for honoring sustained effort — distinct from win or comeback by emphasizing the duration over the outcome.
exemplars: Long-marriage anniversaries; veteran-employee retirement messages; chronic-illness acknowledgment.

name: Naming-the-Gift
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what someone has given
Specific naming of the gift's value
Acknowledgment of what is owed (sometimes nothing)
description: 3-beat shape for honoring someone's contribution — distinct from gratitude by being more analytical about what was given.
exemplars: Retirement tributes; mentor-recognition speeches; intimate-relationship appreciation moments.

name: Holding-Space-for-Anger
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for sitting with someone's anger without escalating, defending, or fixing. Therapeutic and relational core skill.
exemplars: Therapeutic-presence moments; grief-rage acknowledgment; effective conflict-listening.

name: Permission-to-Grieve
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that the loss is real
Specific permission to grieve as long and as hard as needed
description: 3-beat shape for honoring someone's grief without rushing them through it. Distinct from generic sympathy by explicit permission.
exemplars: Compassionate-grief support messages; therapeutic-grief work; community-mourning practices.

name: Refusal-of-Performance
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the expected performance (cheerful, professional, composed)
description: 3-beat shape for refusing to fake okay — distinct from vulnerability share by being explicit about the refusal of expectations.
exemplars: "I'm not okay and won't pretend" messages; refusing-toxic-positivity statements; authentic-leadership moments.

name: Question-as-Care
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what the other is going through
Genuine willingness to receive the answer
description: 3-beat shape for asking a question that is itself a form of care. Distinct from generic inquiry by emotional weight.
exemplars: Skilled care-conversation moves; therapeutic openings; intimate "how are you really?" moments.

name: Telling-Hard-Truth-with-Love
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Re-affirmation of love through the difficulty
description: 3-beat shape for delivering truth that may hurt without rupturing relationship. Distinct from constructive criticism by being more intimate.
exemplars: Family-honesty conversations; close-friend hard-truth moments; intimate-relationship truth-telling.

name: Asking-Better-Question
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that the original question is wrong
Implication of what the better question reveals
description: 3-beat shape for upgrading the question being asked — common in coaching, teaching, journalism. Distinct from refusing-the-frame by being constructive.
exemplars: Coaching-conversation moves; teacher Socratic redirects; journalism-better-question practice.

name: Holding-the-Tension
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Affirmation that staying with tension is the work
description: 3-beat shape for refusing premature resolution. Distinct from holding-two-things by emphasizing the discomfort of the holding.
exemplars: Mature political conversation; long therapeutic work; complex-decision processes.

name: Boundary-Crossed-Named
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that a line has been crossed
What needs to change going forward
description: 3-beat shape for naming a violation in the moment. Distinct from boundary-setting by being responsive to a breach rather than preventive.
exemplars: Workplace-harassment confrontations; intimate-relationship breach moments; community-norm violation calls.

name: Saying-the-Quiet-Part-Loud
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of what's been implied but unsaid
Frame for what to do with the named
description: 3-beat shape for breaking polite avoidance. Distinct from acknowledging-the-elephant by being more confrontational.
exemplars: Bold organizational-honesty moments; relational-truth-telling; political "let's stop pretending..." statements.

name: Owning-Privilege
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the privilege one carries
Specific naming of how it shapes one's perspective
Implication for what to do about it
description: 3-beat shape for honest acknowledgment of structural advantage. Distinct from self-deprecation by being analytical and ongoing.
exemplars: Effective social-justice writing; modern leadership privilege-acknowledgment; ally-positioning statements.

name: Decentering-Self
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that this is not about me
description: 3-beat shape for stepping out of the center of someone else's situation. Distinct from witness-from-outside by being conversational rather than written.
exemplars: Therapeutic moves out of countertransference; conversational re-centering of the other; intimate-relationship listening.

name: Holding-the-Door
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that the door is open
Affirmation that the choice belongs to the recipient
description: 3-beat shape for offering an opportunity without pressure. Distinct from asking by being open-ended and non-coercive.
exemplars: Mentor invitations; reconciliation-availability messages; effective recruiting communications.

name: Witnessing-Growth
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of how far someone has come
Affirmation of who they are now
description: 3-beat shape for honoring someone's transformation. Distinct from compliment by being long-arc and developmental.
exemplars: Mentor-acknowledgment messages; long-friendship recognition; therapeutic-completion moments.

name: Re-affirmation-After-Failure
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
description: 3-beat shape for restoring relationship or commitment after a breach. Distinct from forgiveness by being more about continuation than absolution.
exemplars: Manager-direct-report restoration; relationship-after-rupture conversations; institutional-commitment renewals.

name: Naming-Privilege-of-Listening
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that someone has trusted you with their story
description: 3-beat shape for honoring being entrusted with another's vulnerability. Distinct from validation by acknowledging the gift of being told.
exemplars: Therapeutic-acknowledgment moments; close-friendship trust-naming; mentor-receipt-of-vulnerability.

name: Permission-to-Be-Difficult
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition of the social pressure to be easy
Specific permission to be difficult, complicated, or inconvenient
description: 3-beat shape for releasing someone from performing easiness. Distinct from permission-to-grieve by being more general.
exemplars: Therapeutic-relationship moves; long-friendship messages; self-permission internal monologues.

name: The Quiet Insistence
section: NGC ORIGINALS — Final Communicative Shapes & Closing Inventions
beats: Recognition that the listener may want to dismiss
description: 3-beat shape for not letting something be glossed over. Distinct from doubling down by being gentler and more relational.
exemplars: Therapeutic-confrontation moves; political-truth-telling done patiently; intimate-relationship insistence on what matters.

name: Catalan / Iberian Cant Espiritual (spiritual song-narrative)
description: Iberian (especially Catalan) spiritual narrative-song tradition — Ramon Llull, mystics, modern spiritual poetry. Lyric-narrative spiritual register.
exemplars: Ramon Llull's writings; modern Catalan spiritual poetry (Joan Maragall); Iberian medieval-mystical tradition.

name: Romanian Doina Lament-Narrative
description: Romanian folk lyric-narrative form — solo improvisational vocal lament, deeply place-rooted. UNESCO Intangible Heritage.
exemplars: Maramureș doina; Oltenian doina; modern recordings of traditional doina performers.

name: Albanian Kreshnik Epic
beats: Hero of the kreshnik cycle named
description: Albanian heroic epic tradition — Songs of Frontier Warriors (Kreshnikët), oral narrative of legendary border heroes. Long-line decasyllabic verse.
exemplars: Songs of Mujo and Halil; Albanian National Epic; collections from Northern Albanian highlands.

name: Finnish Kalevala-Form
description: Finnish narrative-poetic form — trochaic tetrameter, alliterative, parallelism. Compiled by Lönnrot (1835) but rooted in much older oral tradition.
exemplars: Elias Lönnrot's Kalevala; Karelian rune-singing tradition; modern Finnish poetic homages.

name: Estonian Kalevipoeg-Form
beats: Encounter with foreign foes or supernatural
description: Estonian national epic form (Kreutzwald, mid-19th c.) — modeled on Kalevala but with distinct Estonian content and register.
exemplars: Kreutzwald's Kalevipoeg; Estonian oral antecedents; modern Estonian narrative poetry.

name: Latvian Daina-Narrative
description: Latvian folk quatrain form — over 1.2 million collected. Compressed narrative-lyric, often agricultural, seasonal, or relational.
exemplars: Latvian dainu folk-tradition; Krišjānis Barons's collections (3rd-largest folk-poem collection in the world).

name: Turkish Halk Hikayesi (folk romance)
description: Turkish folk romance tradition — long oral narrative blending love and adventure. Performed by aşık (folk poet-singers) with saz accompaniment.
exemplars: Köroğlu epic; Aşık Garip; Aşık Kerem; classical Turkish aşık tradition.

name: Hebrew Midrash narrative
beats: Question or gap in the text identified
Return to the text with new understanding
description: Rabbinic Jewish interpretive narrative form — tales spun from biblical gaps, prophetic figures' inner lives, ethical implications. Foundational to Jewish literary tradition.
exemplars: Midrash Rabbah; Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer; Talmudic aggadah; modern midrashic writing.

name: Tibetan Tharpa Liberation Narrative
beats: Return as bodhisattva to help others
description: Tibetan Buddhist liberation-life narrative form — namthar (full hagiography), short tharpa narratives. Spiritual biography genre with specific Buddhist soteriological structure.
exemplars: Milarepa's namthar; Yeshe Tsogyal's life; modern Tibetan Buddhist biography tradition.

name: Sinhala Jātaka-Pota Adaptations
description: Sinhala (Sri Lankan) adaptations of Buddhist Jataka tales — distinguished from Pali Jataka by local cultural details and Sinhala literary conventions.
exemplars: Saddharma-ratnāvaliya (12th c.); Sinhala Jātaka-pota; Sri Lankan Buddhist narrative tradition.

name: The Slow Realization
beats: Acceptance of what was already true
description: Narrative shape for retrospective recognition — what was always there becoming visible. Distinct from realization (746) by emphasizing the accumulation.
